nota: Portada del pilar «Qué es Loop Marketing» (post 248398, fusión con 248483). Fórmula nueva (operador, 2026-10-25): sin persona al frente y sin vidrio. El símbolo del infinito es lo icónico del Loop (operador, 2026-10-26): aquí es una fotografía de luz real, la estela de un péndulo en larga exposición, no el diagrama de HubSpot ni un neón. Las pasadas tenues y abiertas que convergen en una figura nítida dicen que el loop aprende en cada vuelta. Excepción de alcance: §2 caso 4 define Manzanitas por persona; esta portada va sin personas, como la de SEO y AEO (MCB-AEO1-169).

fenomeno.que: a long exposure of a swinging pendulum light over a dark table: its path draws the infinity symbol in light, and the first loose, wide passes, faint, converge into one bright, crisp, closed infinity: each turn of the loop comes out tighter and more precise
fenomeno.esServicio: Loop Marketing: el ciclo que aprende en cada vuelta, a diferencia del embudo que termina

escena: SCENE (cinematic still, Hollywood drama, a vast dark contemporary photo studio at night, a faint trace of haze only on the right of the frame, a cool frame, no people anywhere): a long-exposure photograph looking down at an angle onto a long matte black table. Far from the camera, above the far end of the table, a pendulum hangs from the darkness above the frame on ONE very thin steel wire: only its lowest hand-width, just above the bob, catches a faint grey glint; above that it melts into darkness well below the top edge of the frame. The wire stays one faint hairline, never a fan, a cone or a beam of light. At its end hangs a tiny glowing LED bob. During the long exposure the bob has swung in a figure-eight, and its path is recorded as a continuous ribbon of light floating about fifteen centimetres above the tabletop: the INFINITY SYMBOL, a figure-eight lying flat in the air, two equal, round loops side by side crossing once in the middle; one continuous stroke with no arrowheads, no dots, no breaks and no segments or stages along it. The camera looks DOWN at it from well above the table, about thirty degrees above the table plane, never from table height: in the photograph each loop reads as an almost round open circle with dark tabletop showing through its middle, the whole figure is about twice as wide as it is tall, and it reads instantly as the infinity sign. The figure is FAR from the camera and SMALL in the frame: the whole figure, faint passes included, is SMALL and far: only about one twentieth of the frame width, like a small coin seen across a room; its centre stands seven tenths of the way across the frame from the left edge, well inside the frame and far from the right edge. The table is long and recedes far: its far edge runs across the frame only about one quarter of the way down from the top of the frame, and the figure hovers just in front of that far edge, so the figure sits high in the frame, in its upper third. Beyond the far edge the studio floor falls away into darkness. Everything in the left two thirds of the frame is the bare dark tabletop below and empty darkness above. The ribbon of light is thin, smooth and continuous, like a real light-painting trace: brighter where the bob moved slowly at the outer ends of the loops and thinner and fainter at the crossing, where it moved fast. Around the bright figure lie exactly TWO earlier passes of the same figure-eight, nested just outside it and never more than a finger width away: the FIRST, the widest, slightly uneven and very dim; the SECOND, closer and a little brighter; then the THIRD, the final pass, crisp, closed and bright. All three share the same crossing point: three nested figure-eights, never a spiral, never a coil, never a spirograph pattern, never a tangle of lines. The crisp final infinity is the brightest thing in the frame. The ribbon of light is cold azure-white (#0375DB and cold white): the blue of the frame lives in the trace itself, with a faint azure reflection on the matte tabletop directly under it, never a glow that floods the scene. MOMENT: the exposure closes just as the bob finishes its last, crispest pass. The whole trace, the bob included, is azure-white: there is no other colour in the frame. The light is a real photographic light trail, NOT a neon sign, NOT a tube, NOT a sculpture, NOT a hologram, NOT a graphic, NOT a logo, NOT a drawn line: it has no thickness of its own and casts no shadow. The camera stands about two and a half metres from the figure, raised well above the near end of the table and tilted down toward it, 85mm f/2.8, focused on the figure. The bare matte black tabletop fills the whole lower three quarters of the frame as one calm, even, dark surface receding toward the figure. Between the left edge of the frame and the figure there is a wide band of empty darkness about two thirds of the frame wide; the wire, the figure, its glow and every lit thing stay inside the right third of the frame. Nothing else in the frame: no hand, no person, no device, no screen, no camera, no tripod, no lamps, no books, no plants, no papers, no monitors. There is no face anywhere in this frame: wherever the lighting notes speak of a face, they mean the bright infinity figure against the darkness. The materials are contemporary and clean: matte black table with a fine even surface, no dust, no wear, nothing vintage, nothing warm, amber, orange or golden, no tungsten glow. The whole frame is cool and contemporary. Above the table, the LEFT 64 % of the frame is calm, deep dark space: no light and no objects, no bokeh, no beams. Enormous contrast, no readable text anywhere, no letters, no numbers, no logos of any brand.
